The famous ship that sank in 1912 after hitting an iceberg is the Titanic.

To understand blockchain technology, imagine a massive, shared notebook that is used to record transactions. In a traditional system, like a bank, one central authority holds the only copy of this notebook and decides what gets written in it. However, in a blockchain system, imagine that instead of one notebook, there are thousands of identical notebooks distributed across thousands of different computers around the world.

Every time a new transaction occurs, it is written into a "page" (or block) in all these notebooks simultaneously. Before a page is added, the people holding the other notebooks check the math to ensure the transaction is valid. If the majority agrees it is correct, the page is sealed and added to the chain. Because everyone has a copy, no single person can secretly erase or change a past entry without everyone else noticing and rejecting the change. This makes the record extremely secure and trustworthy, as it relies on collective agreement rather than a single central authority.
